adversarial.a1_channel_capacity: PASS but far narrower than advertised, measured on all 392,318 CA-2023 records. The label does vary with the input (learned AUC 0.95 vs 0.50 for a constant), so unlike the JVM-bytecode kill the channel is not zero. But the headline "12-bit joint mask" carries an empirical joint entropy of only 2.463 bits, against 8.986 bits for independent Bernoullis with the same marginals. Nine of the twelve "most common flags" are health-insurance flags with pairwise correlations 0.843–0.981 (FHICOVP/FPUBCOVP r=0.981, FHICOVP/FPRIVCOVP r=0.972) — they are one event wearing nine hats. Only 324 of 4,096 possible 12-bit patterns occur; the single all-zero pattern is 62.60% of records and the top three are 77.06%. For the full 77-bit mask: 51,818 distinct patterns in 392,318 records, all-zero = 45.59%. So "exact-match over 2^77" overstates the real target by roughly 3.6x even on the 12-bit version, and the proposal's joint-exact-match headline is largely a restatement of the base rate.
adversarial.a2_dumb_baseline: FAIL, decisively, measured. The proposal's two dumb rules ("value is zero/blank", "value equals the mode") were straw men guaranteed to fail because hot-deck donors are real reported values — that is why they scored at or below chance. The rule a survey methodologist would actually write first is: READ THE NONRESPONSE CODES ALREADY PRINTED ON THE RECORD. (1) ONE equality test, `ANC == 4`, zero training records: mean AUC 0.8026 across six representative flags (FPINCP 0.6921, FHICOVP 0.7702, FWAGP 0.7495, FSCHLP 0.8786, FESRP 0.8632, FMARP 0.8622). (2) An eight-line rule = count of the eight published "did not report" indicators, zero training records, evaluated on a household-grouped held-out split (86,068 persons / 35,108 households): mean AUC 0.8297, per-flag FESRP 0.9439, FMARP 0.8939, FWAGP 0.8585; Hamming 0.0915 vs constant 0.1722; joint 6-bit exact-match 0.6510 vs constant 0.6073. (3) On the proposal's own 12 flags over all of CA: mean AUC 0.7480, exact-12 0.7165, Hamming 0.1243 — against their reported learned HistGradientBoosting at n=100,000 of exact-12 0.7280 / Hamming 0.0953 and a constant's 0.6235 / 0.2154. So 100,000 training records buy +0.0115 exact-match over a rule with ZERO training records, and that rule beats their learned model at every n below ~30,000. The mechanism is exact and verifiable: ACS never imputes ancestry (FANCP fires on 0 of 392,318 records), so ANC=4 is a pure unimputed nonresponse marker sitting in X, and item nonresponse clusters hard within respondent — likewise NWLK=3 ".Did not report" predicts FESRP at AUC 0.7398 while the derived ESR recode is allocated and flagged. The round-1 COBOL failure mode the proposal called "decisively absent" is present and worse: there the dumb rule was 50 lines and reached F1 0.768; here it is one line and reaches mean AUC 0.803.
adversarial.confidence: High. Every decisive claim is a measurement on the real corpus, not an argument: 392,318 California person records plus Oregon 2019 and 2023 downloaded and processed this session, a household-grouped split so no household spans train and test, and a documented per-term decomposition of the dumb rule (the NW* terms are confounded with age<16 at r = -0.44 to -0.88 and I report that; ANC==4 is confounded at only r = +0.076 and carries the result alone). The G2a falsification is a direct quotation from the official Census data dictionary, not an inference. The one number I did NOT measure is the extrapolated asymptote (0.958 leaky / 0.865 de-leaked), which is a geometric fit to three measured decades and is labelled as such; the fit predicted the 3.06e5 rungs to within 0.003 and 0.012 before they landed. Two residual uncertainties, neither of which changes the verdict: I did not test the person-plus-household joint framing the proposal names as its fallback (it would add correlated-unit signal but also demands the household-grouped split I already used, and it does not touch the G5 hole), and Semantic Scholar rate-limited me twice so my white-space evidence leans on Crossref, arXiv, dblp, Europe PMC and HuggingFace. A NARROWED version does exist and I want it recorded fairly — "hot-deck footprint detection", i.e. the de-leaked task with all ten nonresponse markers deleted — and it would genuinely PASS G2a and A2 and has a livelier curve than the full version. I still reject it, because it dies on the same G5 wall (both the Census and IPUMS publish the label for free, everywhere) and because its honest numbers are AUC 0.82 and a joint exact-match tied with a constant, which is not a fundable scaling curve.
adversarial.domain: AllocTrace — recovering the Census edit-and-imputation (allocation) mask from released ACS PUMS person microdata
adversarial.g1_licence_reality: PASS — this is the candidate's one unambiguous strength and it is real. https://www2.census.gov/robots.txt returns `User-agent: *` with NO Disallow line (only named crawlers RavenCrawler/MegaIndex/BLP_bbot/TweetmemeBot are blocked, plus crawl-delays for Applebot/Googlebot/Slurp/bingbot); there is no Content-Signal header and no ai-train restriction — the opposite of the Maven Central finding that killed the round-1 bytecode candidate. I verified live fetches: HTTP 200 with content-type application/zip on https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/data/pums/2023/1-Year/csv_pwy.zip, and I actually downloaded and unpacked 2015/2019/2023 Oregon (csv_por.zip) plus the 2023 California file already on disk (69,791,730 bytes, 392,318 person records, 287 columns, 77 contiguous allocation flags FAGEP..FYOEP). These are US federal government works and therefore carry no copyright under 17 USC 105; IPUMS, NBER and others redistribute PUMS routinely. The only restrictive terms I found are on the Census Data API (https://www.census.gov/data/developers/about/terms-of-service.html): a re-identification prohibition ("will not use these data, alone or in combination with any other Census or non-Census data, to identify any individual person, household, business or other entity") and an attribution notice requirement. Neither bars AI training nor redistribution, and neither governs the www2 bulk files. Shipping an open artifact in Phase 3 is legally clean.
adversarial.g2a_what_manufacturer_knows: In principle the Bureau's hot-deck system saw the blank questionnaire box, but I verified line-by-line in the official 2023 ACS PUMS Data Dictionary that the released record REPUBLISHES that blank for ten of the 130 input columns — ANC=4 / ANC1P=999 / ANC2P=999 ".Not reported", DRAT=6 ".Not reported", WRK=b ".N/A (not reported)", and the five variables the dictionary itself labels "(UNEDITED — See 'Employment Status Recode')" NWAB=3, NWAV=5, NWLA=3, NWLK=3, NWRE=3 each ".Did not report" — so the manufacturer's supposedly privileged view of "which boxes the respondent left empty" is printed directly on the student's input, and the proposal's central G2a sentence ("the student sees only the post-imputation record in which every field is populated and internally consistent") is factually false.
adversarial.g3_kill_attempt: Two attacks. (A) DELETE THE LEAK: retrain HistGradientBoosting with the ten published nonresponse-marker columns removed (ANC, ANC1P, ANC2P, WRK, NWAB, NWAV, NWLA, NWLK, NWRE, plus ESR/MSP/OC/RC/PAOC/NOP/DECADE), household-grouped split, six representative flags. Leaky model: 0.9082 / 0.9342 / 0.9467 / 0.9492 mean AUC at n = 1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5 / 3.06e5. De-leaked model: 0.6821 / 0.7635 / 0.8087 / 0.8202 at the same rungs — it collapses by 0.226 AUC at n=1e3. Almost the entire advertised result is the leak. (B) FIT THE CURVE: leaky per-decade increments decay at rho=0.481, giving a geometric tail of +0.0116 beyond 1e5 and an asymptote near 0.958 — meaning the curve is 97.5% COMPLETE AT n=1e5, before the first rung of the intended 1e6 range; the last half-decade (1e5 to 3.06e5) buys +0.0025. The de-leaked curve decays at rho=0.555, asymptote ~0.865, 84.5% complete at 1e5, and its half-decade 1e5 to 3.06e5 buys +0.0115. Worse, the de-leaked model's joint 6-bit exact-match at 306,250 training records is 0.6081 — statistically indistinguishable from the constant predictor's 0.6073, i.e. after a third of a million examples it still cannot beat "always predict not-allocated" on the joint mask. (C) TRANSFER: I downloaded Oregon 1-Year PUMS for 2019 and 2023 and tested cross-state and cross-year. CA2023 100k -> OR2023 = 0.9383, CA2023 100k -> OR2019 = 0.9281, OR2019 40k -> OR2023 = 0.9318, versus OR2023 30k -> OR2023 held-out = 0.9699. Transfer is nearly free, which is superficially good for the abundance claim but is further evidence the signal is a generic low-dimensional nonresponse-propensity latent, not a rich dataset-specific hot-deck footprint that would reward 1e6 examples.
adversarial.g3_survives: Two things survive honestly and I want them on the record. First, the proposal is RIGHT that a frontier model with plain prompting cannot eat this: the input is 130 integer survey codes with no natural-language surface, and the founder's specific historical failure mode is genuinely unavailable to an attacker here. The attacker that actually kills it is not a bigger model, it is `sum of eight equality tests`. Second, there IS a real residual signal once the leak is removed — the de-leaked curve rises monotonically 0.6821 -> 0.7635 -> 0.8087 -> 0.8202 with no reversal, and its per-decade increments (+0.081, +0.045) are LIVELIER than the leaky model's (+0.026, +0.013). That residual is the genuinely FDM-1-shaped part of the idea: joint implausibility of a hot-deck donor value against the rest of the record. But it is still 84.5% exhausted at 1e5, it cannot beat a constant on the joint mask, and it is a much smaller effect than the headline. G3 fails on headroom, not on the prompting argument.
adversarial.g4_recheck: White space PASS, crowding ~2/10 — the proposal's G4 claim holds and I could not break it. Nine formulations across arXiv API, Crossref, dblp, Semantic Scholar (429 rate-limited on two attempts, noted), Europe PMC, HuggingFace datasets API, and one WebSearch; two domain venues reached (Journal of Official Statistics via Crossref; FCSM). HuggingFace returned ZERO datasets for "acs pums", "allocation flag", and "census microdata" (endpoint verified working — "census" returns scikit-learn/adult-census-income). No paper trains a model to produce the flags. BUT the G4 pass is hollow and one new find explains why, and it is a G5 problem, not a G4 one: (1) T. Kirk White, "Recovering the Item-Level Edit and Imputation Flags in the 1977-1997 Censuses of Manufactures", 2015, DOI 10.2139/ssrn.2572670 — the title IS the task, but the Crossref abstract shows the method is ARCHIVAL, not predictive: "reconstructing the edit/imputation flags for variables in the 1977, 1982, 1987, 1992, and 1997 Censuses of Manufactures using recently recovered Census Bureau files." When a statistical agency wants missing imputation flags, the accepted and successful remedy is to go find the original file. (2) Decisive: IPUMS USA — one of the two NAMED BUYERS — already publishes per-variable data quality flags for every sample back to 1850 (https://usa.ipums.org/usa-action/variables/QAGE, https://usa.ipums.org/usa/flags.shtml), and where source flags never existed IPUMS MANUFACTURES them itself with documented procedures ("3 - Logical computer edit by IPUMS", "4 - Hot deck allocation by IPUMS"). The Census publishes the F* flags; IPUMS publishes Q* flags everywhere the F* flags are absent. There is no microdata product in the named buyers' inventory that lacks this label. Nobody has built this because the label ships free from both the producer and the redistributor.
adversarial.g6_reasoning: Not the constraint; comfortably within the 4-core/15GB/no-GPU/30GB box. Measured on the real file: 130 feature codes at int16 = 260 B/unit (ADJINC needs int32, trivially handled), plus a packed 77-bit mask at 10 B = 270 B/unit. Corpus at 1e3/1e4/1e5/1e6/1e7 units = 0.3 MB / 2.7 MB / 27 MB / 270 MB / 2.7 GB, all resident in 15 GB. Raw bulk is ~24 GB zipped for 50 states x 20 years, which is tight against ~22 GB free but streams state-by-state. Empirically, this session trained 6 HistGradientBoosting heads x 4 rungs up to n=306,250 on 130 features in roughly 25 minutes on 2 threads while two other agents' jobs were saturating the box (load average 10+ on 4 cores). Scaling to 77 heads x 4 rungs x 1e6 is a small number of CPU-hours. If this candidate died, it did not die on G6.
adversarial.strongest_case_against: The advertised result is leakage, and the leak is not subtle — it is printed in the codebook. The proposal's G2a sentence asserts the student sees a record "in which every field is populated and internally consistent"; the official 2023 ACS PUMS Data Dictionary says otherwise for ten of the 130 input columns, five of which the dictionary itself stamps "(UNEDITED)". Because ACS never imputes ancestry (FANCP fires on 0 of 392,318 records) it simply publishes ANC=4 ".Not reported" verbatim, and because item nonresponse clusters within respondent, that single published code predicts allocation of OTHER items at mean AUC 0.8026 with a one-line rule and zero training data — inside the proposal's own quoted "learned 0.886–0.939" band on several flags (FESRP 0.9439 for the eight-line version). Delete those ten columns and the model falls from 0.9082 to 0.6821 at n=1e3, and at n=306,250 its joint 6-bit exact-match is 0.6081 against a constant predictor's 0.6073 — a third of a million examples cannot beat "always predict not-allocated". Meanwhile the leaky curve is 97.5% complete at n=1e5 and the de-leaked curve 84.5% complete, so the two orders of magnitude the thesis is built on buy roughly +0.01 and +0.05 AUC respectively. And the economic tail is empty in a way that cannot be engineered around: the label is a published column in the same free CSV, IPUMS already ships equivalent Q-flags for every sample back to 1850 and manufactures them where they never existed, and White (2015) shows that when a statistical agency actually needs missing imputation flags it recovers the archived file rather than training a predictor. The proposal deserves credit for stating its own weakness honestly ("the curve is decelerating hard... if those also flatten by 1e5, kill it rather than defend it") — I ran exactly that test a day early, and they flatten.

The label varies with the SUBMITTER and the CALENDAR, not with the input. Galaxy Version 3.12.0" / "SPAdes v. 3.12.0"). The proposer's "3,517 distinct version strings and that is the number that matters" is predominantly typographic noise.
adversarial.a2_dumb_baseline: THE PROPOSER MEASURED THE WRONG BASELINE. The dumbest non-learned rule is not QUAST — it is ~15 lines of regex over the submitter's ORIGINAL contig names, which GenBank preserves verbatim in the definition line and which NCBI serves for free from the same Datasets endpoint (/genome/accession/{acc}/sequence_reports -> "sequence_name"). Those names ARE the assembler's own output convention: NODE_1_length_905814_cov_25.560276 (SPAdes/Velvet — and it PRINTS THE COVERAGE REGRESSION TARGET), SAMN45839652-rid25664583.denovo.01 (SKESA/NCBI Pathogen Detection), tig00000001 (Canu), k127_100 (MEGAHIT — and it prints k), contig00001 (Shovill), adZHK-supercont1.1 (ALLPATHS-LG), ERS1580622SCcontig000001 (Sanger/Prokka). MEASURED on 2,999 S. aureus assemblies across 603 bioprojects / 291 submitters, 20-class assembler family: bare regex, abstention scored as wrong, 0.5603 ACC with 0.8677 precision on the 64.6% where it fires. Under a SUBMITTER-grouped split: QUAST contiguity stats alone 0.3813 ACC / 0.1431 balACC; defline regex indicators alone 0.6251 / 0.2294; QUAST + defline (the actual free incumbent) 0.6883 ACC. Under a bioproject-grouped split: 0.3560 / 0.6078 / 0.6767. So the regex adds ~30 accuracy points over the baseline the proposer reported as "the honest dumb baseline, the rules-plus-QUAST incumbent" — and the proposer's claimed 26 points of family headroom is measured against a baseline that omits the single most informative free feature in the record.
adversarial.confidence: High on the fine-grained targets (version, technology, coverage): the kill rests on a primary-source changelog, a same-software negative control that scores as high as the real pairs, a fake-label control, and a temporal split where the model loses to a constant — four independent lines that agree. High on G6 (measured bytes, arithmetic). Medium-high on the domain as a whole: the family-only narrowing has real but thin capacity, and its buyer already owns the free tool that captures most of it. Medium on my one untested flank, the base-level sequence, for the reason stated above. Note also that a narrowed AssemblyProv-family study would still have to publish its headline as a ~20-class balanced accuracy under a submitter-grouped split, against a free incumbent at 0.688 ACC, over a corpus whose label information saturates at ~10^5 independent groups — that is not a scaling-curve story, it is a 1.5-order-of-magnitude story with a strong non-learned competitor, so I do not recommend it even as a backup.
adversarial.domain: AssemblyProv — recovering assembler software/version, sequencing technology and read coverage from a deposited prokaryotic genome assembly (NCBI GenBank)
adversarial.g1_licence_reality: PASS, and it is the only clean pass. Nor do we accept data when the submitter has requested restrictions on reuse or redistribution." Redistribution of a derived open dataset is therefore permitted. The proposer's numbers come from a random split, but the label is a project-level constant: 97.4% of the 5,918 S. aureus bioprojects carry exactly ONE method string, and "predict method = most common method of this bioproject" scores 0.9553 with zero sequence involved; release-month alone scores 0.6867 against a 0.4797 majority. Switching only the split: bioproject-grouped 0.5187 / 0.2176; full-method-string random 0.7117 -> grouped 0.3892; and on a temporal split the full-method model scores 0.7630 against a train-majority constant at 0.7770 — it LOSES to a constant. adversarial.g6_reasoning: Measured over 41 real Datasets-API downloads: mean 829 KB, median 827 KB of compressed FASTA per assembly. Rungs: 1k = 0.8 GB, 10k = 8.3 GB, 100k = 83 GB, 1M = 829 GB, against a 30 GB disk. Two-bit packing does not save it — mean S. aureus assembly is 2.85 Mbp = 0.71 MB packed, so 100k = 71 GB and 1M = 713 GB. The 100k rung is already 2.4-2.8x over disk and the 1M rung is 24-28x over, so half the required scaling curve cannot be built on the stated box with the stated input ("contigs as ACGTN strings"). The only representation that does fit is the compaction the proposer calls mandatory — a contig-length list is 0.2 KB/genome, 0.2 GB at 1M — and that is exactly the representation I tested and found to sit inside the confound floor for the fine label. So the box forces the representation that has no measured capacity, and the representation that might have capacity does not fit the box. (Streaming-and-discarding would mean fixing hand-designed features in advance, which contradicts the sequence-model thesis, and re-pulling ~800 GB from NCBI per epoch is not a viable training loop.)
adversarial.strongest_case_against: The strongest case for selecting it anyway, which I want on the record because it is the one thing my kill does not fully close: my A1 measurement used the contig-LENGTH multiset, not the bases. The published mechanism for a non-zero channel (Rahman & Pachter, Genome Research 2022, on unsafe-unitig misassembly and bidirected-graph underassembly) lives in base-level structure — repeat-collapse boundaries, the exact junction where the assembler gave up — which a length multiset cannot see. A sequence model over raw bases could in principle find signal I did not test for. Three things blunt this. First, the changelog evidence is representation-independent: if SPAdes 3.13.0 and 3.13.1 execute the identical code on a bacterial isolate, no representation recovers a difference that was never written. Second, the effective-N result (122,550 bioprojects, 97.4% single-method, top 8 projects = 41% of the archive) and the temporal-split result (model loses to a constant) are also representation-independent. Third, testing the rebuttal costs 83-829 GB on a 30 GB box. If someone insists, the cheap decisive experiment is ~500 SPAdes 3.13.0 and ~500 SPAdes 3.13.1 bacterial assemblies from disjoint submitters, full FASTA, any sequence model, submitter-grouped: the changelog predicts 0.500, and I measured 0.566 +- 0.069 from lengths. A second, more honest fallback exists — install two SPAdes versions and assemble one public read set with each, the direct javac-345/345 test — but SPAdes 3.13.x on 4 cores / 15 GB is hours per run and I judged the changelog plus the negative control to be the stronger evidence per hour.

all_candidates.a1_channel_capacity: The residual demonstrably varies: RESORB is specified at ~10 cm radial accuracy and POEORB at ~5 cm 3-D, so the difference is a real, non-zero, epoch-varying signal driven by mismodelled drag, solar radiation pressure and onboard GPS clock behaviour, all of which vary with solar activity, eclipse geometry and orbit position. Unlike the javac case, the two products come from different filters with different observability, so byte-identity is impossible by construction. I did NOT download and difference a real file pair, so residual magnitude and structure are UNVERIFIED.
all_candidates.a2_dumb_baseline: This is the candidate's biggest weakness and I will not soften it. Honestly I estimate that table captures roughly half the variance of |SISRE| and is close to what industry uses today. The learnable margin is specifically the conditional TAIL — the 99.9th-percentile bound that drives protection levels — where URA is a loose per-satellite constant that does not track eclipse, upload cadence, or clock-model drift. all_candidates.a1_channel_capacity: PLAUSIBLE but NOT MEASURED by me, which is this candidate's biggest open risk. The mechanistic argument: k-mer size and coverage cut-off determine exactly where the assembly graph was broken, so contig boundary sequence, repeat-collapse behaviour, minimum retained contig length and the small-contig tail are direct imprints of the generator. Different assemblers demonstrably produce different contig sets from identical reads. But I did not run the experiment, and the honest lesson from round 1 is that this class of claim must be measured before it is believed.
all_candidates.a2_dumb_baseline: HONEST, AND IT PARTLY BITES. The dumbest rule set — thresholds on contig count, N50, minimum contig length, and presence of N-runs — recovers a lot. 'One circular contig => long-read assembler (Flye/Canu/Unicycler)' and 'N-runs present => scaffolded' probably get most of the Sequencing Technology label and a fair slice of assembler FAMILY. Worse, the minimum-contig-length floor is a near-giveaway (SPAdes defaults to 128bp, SKESA to 200bp) and that is a one-line rule. My honest estimate is that dumb rules get the technology label largely and assembler family perhaps half. What they should NOT get is assembler VERSION, and they should get essentially nothing on Genome Coverage as a regression target — the surviving task is the fine-grained one, and the coarse one must be discarded rather than reported as a win.

g4_results.domain: EphemErr — GNSS broadcast-ephemeris error nowcasting (predict per-record orbit/clock error and the conditional upper quantile of SISRE from the broadcast navigation message, with post-processed SP3/CLK as truth)
g4_results.g4_reasoning:
G4 fails on both clauses, and it fails because the round-1 reconnaissance searched the wrong indexes. dblp and arXiv genuinely return almost nothing here — but that is a property of dblp's CS scope and of a community that does not preprint, not a property of the field. The moment I queried the navigation community's own publishers directly (Crossref DOI prefix 10.33012, which is the Institute of Navigation; the GPS Solutions journal endpoint; Europe PMC, which indexes the MDPI Sensors/Remote Sensing corpus where this field actually publishes), the white space evaporated.

EFFORT COUNT: at least seven serious efforts, in two distinct clusters, against a PASS threshold of three.

Cluster 1 — the candidate's PRIMARY target (conditional upper quantile of SISRE) is the subject of a continuous, standardised, aviation-certification-grade research programme running 2010-2025 under the name SISRE overbounding / ARAIM Integrity Support Message generation. I pulled the full abstract of the nearest item, ION GNSS+ 2022 DOI 10.33012/2022.18306, and it does not merely characterise the aggregate: it bootstraps the distribution of the MAXIMUM projected clock+ephemeris error and explicitly 'partition[s] the data for different observable conditions ... to determine whether the current bounding behavior is representative of future data.' That is conditional upper-quantile estimation of SISRE, performed by stratification instead of by a learned model. Around it sit ION ITM 2023 (18606), ION GNSS+ 2020 (17577), ION GNSS+ 2019 (16938), NAVIGATION 2020 (navi.346), IEEE TAES 2023, IEEE/ION PLANS 2020, and GPS Solutions 2023 (s10291-023-01525-2). The incumbent is not a gap; it is a deployed standard with a working group attached.

Cluster 2 — learned per-satellite modelling of broadcast ephemeris error is independently replicated by at least five groups since 2021: Remote Sensing 2021 (BP/PSO-BP, 30-50% RMS3D improvement), Comput. Intell. Neurosci. 2022 (BDS-3 PSO+BP), Sensors 2022 (LSTM on IGS RTS orbit corrections specifically across the IOD/upload boundary — which is the exact feature EphemErr proposes to exploit), SPIE ICGRSM 2024, IEEE ICAACE 2026, plus a 2024 RNN preprint. Sensors 2022 is the most damaging: it is a learned model, conditioned on the upload discontinuity, predicting the correction to the broadcast orbit.

OPEN DATASET: the second clause also fails. BDSet (Scientific Data 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-07032-6) is an open, DOI'd, continuously-updated 142.7 GB / ~255 million-message corpus of decoded PPP-B2b SSR corrections — per-satellite orbit and clock corrections to the BDS broadcast ephemeris, i.e. a close proxy for the candidate's label at well above 10^6 pairs. It is not identical (real-time ground-segment estimate rather than post-processed SP3 truth, BDS only), so on its own it would argue MARGINAL. Combined with the effort count it does not rescue the verdict.

TWO FURTHER PROBLEMS I HIT WHILE VERIFYING, WORTH RECORDING EVEN THOUGH G4 WAS MY REMIT:

A2 (heuristic-shaped labels) looks fatal independently. The dumbest non-learned baseline here is a lookup table keyed on two fields that are already IN the broadcast record: the URA/SISA index — a field whose entire designed purpose is to declare the expected magnitude of this exact error — and age-of-data since toe. Error growth with age-of-data is the single best-characterised effect in the literature. A per-(satellite-block, URA-index, AOD-bin) empirical quantile table would capture most of the signal, and the ARAIM ISM pipeline already builds precisely that table. The ION 2022 result that 'most of the standard deviations are below the user range accuracy' is a direct measurement that the broadcast URA field alone already overbounds the error most of the time. This is the COBOL 50-line-baseline failure mode, and the incumbent baseline here is not a strawman I would have to build — it is certified and deployed.

G2 moat: the label manufacturer is commodity tooling. RTKLIB and GNSSTk both ship broadcast-ephemeris evaluation and SP3-c precise interpolation; the EUREF/EPN community publishes routine broadcast-vs-precise runs; GPS Solutions 2018 already reports an 18-year BRDC-vs-precise study across four IGS data centres. The differencing pipeline is an afternoon's work for anyone in the field, which means no data moat accrues from building it.

G2a (information asymmetry) is the one gate the candidate passes cleanly and it is genuinely well-argued — the manufacturer sees the reconstructed truth from a ~500-station network days later, the student sees only the forward prediction. That asymmetry is real. It is simply not enough when the resulting problem is already owned twice over.

RECOMMENDATION: kill. Do not attempt to rescue this by narrowing the framing to 'learned conditional quantile, nav-record-only input, at 10^6 scale.' That delta is a method contribution inside an occupied, standardised problem, not a domain with white space — and the aviation buyer, the one with real money, cannot accept a learned tail bound in place of a certified statistical one, so the method delta and the economic tail point in opposite directions.

g4_results.g4_reasoning:
Three independent serious efforts do precisely this task, and the composition is worse than the count. (1) Brunner & Sippel, Environmental Data Science 2023, run 47-way classification over 43 CMIP6 models from single daily metadata-stripped temperature maps — the proposed task at nearly the proposed class cardinality — and release MIT-licensed code plus PRE-TRAINED classifiers and a Zenodo deposit. (2) Yiou & Thao, npj Climate and Atmospheric Science 2025, is a Nature-family paper published this year whose title is a near-verbatim restatement of the proposed headline: 'Using artificial intelligence to identify CMIP6 models from daily SLP maps'. It even harvests the model-family structure from the classifier's confusions, which is the genealogy angle. (3) Labe & Barnes, Earth and Space Science 2022, founded the framing with a 7-GCM Arctic classifier plus LRP. A reviewer does not need to search; the near-duplicate is in a Nature journal from the current year.

Strict arithmetic puts this at exactly the 3-effort MARGINAL boundary, and no open dataset ships 10^6 labelled (field, source_id) pairs under that exact label. I am calling FAIL anyway for three measured reasons.

First, the shipped-artifact contribution is already built. ClimDetect (HuggingFace, CC-BY-4.0, 1,272,212 rows) is CMIP6 daily fields regridded to a uniform 64x128 grid with provenance stripped down to (input, target, year) — that is the proposed corpus construction, at the proposed scale, already open, with the CMIP6 model list shipped alongside as Clim_Detect_ds_info.csv and the pipeline released. ClimateSet (NeurIPS 2023 D&B, 36 models) is organised by source model, so labelled pairs fall out for free. Phase 3's open artifact would be a groupby on someone else's release.

Second, the incumbents' own numbers show the quality curve saturates orders of magnitude below rung 4, which is the thing the founder cannot be caught shipping. Brunner & Sippel get 99.4% on the binary task with LOGISTIC REGRESSION — a linear model is the dumbest learned baseline there is, and it nearly solves it. Labe & Barnes hit 100% test accuracy with a 2,016 -> 10 -> 10 -> 7 MLP on 840 training maps. Brunner & Sippel themselves write that more samples 'would SLOWLY improve the classification skill even further' — the incumbents have stated the scaling hypothesis and pre-characterised it as flat. The 47-class daily version at 83.4% leaves headroom, so the curve is not provably dead, but a study whose deliverable IS the scaling curve cannot start from a lane where a linear model already scores 99.4% at 2k samples per class.

Third, the buyer story does not survive the practitioner check. CF conventions plus the CMIP6 'ripf' variant identifier uniquely tag every ensemble member, ES-DOC provides standardised model documentation and an errata service, and ESGF publishes checksums. Orphaned-provenance is solved administratively and exactly, not probabilistically — I found no practitioner thread describing it as an open problem.

Two secondary notes for the record. G1 is unresolved and is a real risk: CMIP6 defaults to CC BY-SA 4.0 per modelling centre with some centres on CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and the SHARE-ALIKE clause propagates to derivatives, so a mixed-source corpus inherits the most restrictive terms. I could not measure the per-model split because esgf-node.llnl.gov/esg-search now 302-redirects to esgf-node.ornl.gov/esgf-1-5-bridge. Separately, G2a is weaker than the brief claims: the ensemble-member/initial-condition half of the label is unrecoverable in principle from a single slice, which is not information asymmetry, it is an unlearnable target — the manufacturer knows something the student cannot ever recover, so that portion of the label is noise, not signal, and it caps the achievable curve rather than lifting it. Only source_id is genuinely learnable, and that is the exact 47-class problem Brunner & Sippel published in 2023.

Searched 15 formulations across 14 venues, including three domain-specific ones (PCMDI/WCRP CMIP6 standards, the EGU General Assembly programme via Copernicus meetingorganizer, and the ESGF data infrastructure) plus the field's own journals (Environmental Data Science, npj Climate and Atmospheric Science, Earth and Space Science, GRL, Earth System Dynamics, GMD). arXiv and dblp returned literal zeros, which initially reads as white space but is an artifact of where this community publishes — the work is all in Copernicus, AGU and Cambridge venues, and it is there.

serious_efforts.name: Brunner & Sippel — 'Identifying climate models based on their daily output using machine learning', Environmental Data Science
serious_efforts.scale: 43 CMIP6 models + 4 obs = 47 classes; 2,000 daily samples per dataset for multi-class (~94k pairs); 2.5deg grid, 6,888 ocean cells
serious_efforts.what_it_did: THIS IS THE TASK, at essentially the proposed class cardinality. 47-way classification (43 CMIP6 models + 4 observational products) of daily 2m air-temperature maps with all provenance removed. Logistic regression and an 8-hidden-layer CNN. 83.4% overall multi-class accuracy, 69.9% on out-of-period 2091-2100 projections; 99.4% (LR) / 99.7% (CNN) on the binary model-vs-observation version. Both temporally out-of-sample and dataset-out-of-sample protocols. Ships MIT-licensed code AND pre-trained classifiers at github.com/lukasbrunner/model_learning plus a Zenodo deposit. Explicitly states 'it can be assumed that increasing the number of training samples would slowly improve the classification skill even further' — the incumbents have already articulated the scaling hypothesis and characterised it as SLOW.

serious_efforts.name: Yiou & Thao — 'Using artificial intelligence to identify CMIP6 models from daily SLP maps', npj Climate and Atmospheric Science
serious_efforts.scale: CMIP6 ensemble, daily SLP over the North Atlantic, multi-model multi-class; 0 citations as of this search (published 2025)
serious_efforts.what_it_did: The near-duplicate named in the mission brief, and it is worse than expected: a Nature-family journal, published this year, whose title is a near-verbatim statement of the proposed headline task. Neural networks distinguish CMIP6 models from daily sea-level-pressure maps over the North Atlantic; finds models are highly identifiable in summer and less so in other seasons; recovers model FAMILIES (i.e. genealogy structure) from the classifier's confusions; projects how identifiability shifts by end of century; uses layer-wise relevance propagation for attribution. Frames the motivation as model selection for AI-based forecasting.

serious_efforts.name: Labe & Barnes — 'Comparison of Climate Model Large Ensembles With Observations in the Arctic Using Simple Neural Networks', Earth and Space Science
serious_efforts.scale: 7 GCM classes (CanESM2, MPI, CSIRO-MK3.6, EC-Earth, GFDL-CM3, GFDL-ESM2M, LENS); 840 training maps; network is 2,016 -> 10 -> 10 -> 7 softmax; reports 100% test accuracy
serious_efforts.what_it_did: Trains an ANN to classify which of 7 GCM large ensembles produced each annual-mean Arctic near-surface-temperature map, then feeds observations in and ranks models by the classifier's confidence. Uses layer-wise relevance propagation to expose which grid cells carry the model's signature. The founding paper of the 'which model made this field' framing in the AGU literature, and the direct methodological ancestor of both efforts above. Code and figures at zenodo.org/record/6564106.

known_limitations: The round-2 pipeline returned the adversarial payload for surviving candidates but did not carry their G4 payload through the pipeline stage, so the recorded g4_results contain only the two candidates whose G4 verdict was FAIL (EphemErr, ModelPrint-CMIP). The G4 verdicts for AllocTrace and AssemblyProv are referenced inside their adversarial reviews but their full search records were not returned. This is a harness defect, recorded rather than hidden.

AssemblyProv's adversary explicitly recorded the one thing its kill does not close: the A1 measurement used the contig-LENGTH multiset, not the bases, and the published mechanism for a non-zero channel lives in base-level structure. It also named the cheap decisive experiment (~500 SPAdes 3.13.0 vs ~500 3.13.1 bacterial assemblies from disjoint submitters, submitter-grouped) and the reason it was not run (83-829 GB against a 30 GB disk).

The AllocTrace 'de-leaked' residual is real and rises monotonically (0.6821 -> 0.7635 -> 0.8087 -> 0.8202 mean AUC across 1e3/1e4/1e5/3.06e5) with livelier per-decade increments than the leaky model. It was rejected on headroom and on an empty economic tail, not on the absence of signal.

round1_leftovers_attacked.a1_channel_capacity: MEASURED, AND IT IS THE JAVAC FINDING AGAIN. I downloaded Debian bookworm packages for 8 architectures (amd64, i386, arm64, armhf, armel, mips64el, ppc64el, s390x — riscv64 404s on bookworm) and parsed 838 real ELFs with pyelftools; separately 3,215 ELFs from the local Ubuntu 24.04 root. Base address = min PT_LOAD p_vaddr. Result on the 838 multi-arch set: 7 distinct values ever observed, 0x0 = 98.45%, H(base) = 0.1518 bits. On the 3,215-file set: 4 distinct values, 0x0 = 98.26%, H(base) = 0.1451 bits. Conditioning on the architecture (which ISAdetect already recovers at ~98%) leaves H(base | ISA) = 0.1076 bits, and 8 of the 11 arch classes have H exactly 0. Steelmanning with non-PIE only (ET_EXEC, n=65) it rises to just H = 1.89 bits over 8 distinct values, mode-predictor 50.8%. Weak corroboration on PE: only 3 PE files were reachable in my corpus, all ImageBase 0x400000 — COULD NOT VERIFY at Assemblage's 890k PE scale, but MSVC ImageBase is a documented linker constant (0x400000 / 0x10000000 / 0x140000000 / 0x180000000), so the same degeneracy is expected. The base-address label — the half round 1 hoped was the uncrowded one — is not a function of the input; it is a linker constant carrying about one tenth of one bit. The ISA half by contrast carries H = 2.91 bits and code/data segmentation is genuinely high-entropy, so the bundle is not uniformly zero-capacity — but the two halves that DO carry bits die on A2 and G4 respectively.
round1_leftovers_attacked.a2_dumb_baseline: THREE DUMB BASELINES, ALL MEASURED ON THIS BOX. (1) Base address, dumbest possible: "always predict 0x0" → 98.45% exact on 838 multi-arch Debian ELFs. (2) Base address, dumb-but-content-aware, ~35 lines, the classic pointer-histogram idea: unpack every word, histogram by page, slide a window of the image's page-width, take the max. On 23 non-PIE nonzero-base ELFs, with zero tuning: 34.8% exact, 65.2% within one page, 82.6% within 16 KiB, 91.3% within 64 KiB. The published versions of this (literal-pool matching, absolute-address statistics) and binbloom do better. (3) ISA + endianness + word size, nearest-centroid on a 256-bin byte histogram of 8 KiB of .text — no training loop, nothing beyond a per-class mean: 93.91% leave-one-out over 11 classes (majority-class baseline 19.92%), n=723. ISAdetect reports ~98% with a real classifier. (4) Code/data segmentation, dumbest possible ("every loaded byte is code"): 49.87% micro / 55.62% macro byte-accuracy over 837 binaries — this is the ONE sub-task with real residual, and it is exactly LOADSTAR. Worst of all, I measured the scaling curve for the ISA task on held-out n=200: 65.6% @ 8 training examples, 89.6% @ 64, 91.7% @ 128, 91.1% @ 256, 90.3% @ 523. It is FLAT from 128 onward — saturated four orders of magnitude below the 10^6 target. That is the precise opposite of the FDM-1 structure the mission requires.
round1_leftovers_attacked.confidence: High. The three decisive numbers were measured on this box in under an hour on real data, not argued: H(base) = 0.152 bits over 838 Debian ELFs spanning 8 architectures downloaded live from deb.debian.org; 93.91% LOO ISA accuracy from a nearest-centroid with no training loop; and a scaling curve that is flat from n=128 to n=523 on held-out data. The G4 crowding is confirmed by dblp/Crossref records I fetched, not recalled — including a 2025 IEEE S&P paper using the identical pseudo-label mechanism and six dedicated base-address papers dating to 2016. The only things I could not verify are the PE ImageBase distribution at Assemblage scale (only 3 PE files were reachable in my corpus; all 0x400000, and MSVC defaults imply the same degeneracy but this is inference, not measurement) and Assemblage's per-binary licence composition across its 30,856 source repos. Neither would change the verdict: the ELF measurement alone is fatal, and G4 is independently fatal.
round1_leftovers_attacked.domain: Headerless load-layout recovery: base address, ISA/endianness and code/data segmentation for raw firmware blobs (corpus: Assemblage ELF/PE + Debian; manufacturer shape (c) — delete the ELF/PE header, the header IS the label)
round1_leftovers_attacked.g1_licence_reality: Mixed, and MARGINAL for the Phase-3 shipping requirement. Debian is clean: I actually fetched Packages.gz and ~480 .deb files across 8 architectures from http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/bookworm/main/binary-{amd64,i386,arm64,armhf,armel,mips64el,ppc64el,s390x}/ — all HTTP 200, no robots.txt served at all (404), and Debian main is DFSG-free and explicitly redistributable. Assemblage is the problem: https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/changliu8541/Assemblage_LinuxELF and .../Assemblage_PE both carry cardData {"license": "other"}, tag license:other, ungated, ~375 GB, arxiv:2405.03991. The dataset card states the Assemblage CODE is MIT but "individual binaries retain their original repository licenses" — i.e. there is no blanket redistribution grant covering the 428,884 ELF / 890,000 PE artifacts drawn from 30,856 GitHub repos. Shipping an open artifact derived from that would require a per-repo licence audit across 30,856 repos, a large fraction of which on GitHub carry no licence at all (= all rights reserved). Not fatal on its own — you could build the whole study on Debian main — but it removes the "428k + 890k units" abundance claim as a redistributable corpus, and Debian alone at 10^6 units is a stretch.
round1_leftovers_attacked.g2a_what_manufacturer_knows: The manufacturer reads the e_machine / e_ident / p_vaddr / e_entry / section-table bytes that were physically deleted from the student's copy — a crisp answer, but a degenerate one: unlike VPT's future frames, those bytes are a redundant re-encoding of information still present in the body (absolute pointers, ARM literal pools, the reset vector table, opcode statistics), and a published deterministic algorithm reads it straight back out, so the asymmetry is nominal rather than informational and the ceiling is a solved decoding problem, not a teacher.
round1_leftovers_attacked.g3_kill_attempt: The right kill here is not a frontier model — the input is raw bytes, plain prompting genuinely is not expressible over it, and that part of G3 is fine. The kill is the other clause of G3: an existing NON-LEARNED tool already does this, in production, and the learned curve is measured flat. binbloom (Quarkslab, 585 stars, verified via GitHub) determines loading address AND endianness of raw headerless firmware by heuristic statistics; rbasefind and Ghidra's base-finder do the same; radare2/rabin2 and ISAdetect cover the ISA half. Behind them sits a decade of dedicated algorithms: literal-pool matching (Digital Investigation 2016, 22 cit), image-base determination for ARM (IEICE Trans. 2016, 19 cit), ICS firmware image base (Int. J. Critical Infrastructure Protection 2017, 31 cit), MIPS absolute-address statistics + string reference matching (Computers & Security 2020), function-address matching (WCMC 2021), image-base range (LNNS 2023). My own untuned 35-line reimplementation of the idea hit 91.3% within 64 KiB. A learned model trained on 10^6 units would be competing against a deterministic decoder for a label that carries 0.11 bits conditional on the arch.
round1_leftovers_attacked.g3_survives: Nothing survives intact. The bundle has three sub-tasks and each dies to a different gate, so they do not recombine into a survivor: base address dies on A1 (0.15 bits of label entropy, measured) and on six dedicated published algorithms; ISA/endianness dies on A2 (93.9% from a nearest-centroid with no training loop, curve flat past n=128) and on ISAdetect/ELISA/Clemens; code/data segmentation is the only high-entropy residual and it is precisely "You Can't Judge a Binary by Its Header: Data-Code Separation for Non-Standard ARM Binaries Using Pseudo Labels" (IEEE S&P 2025) — the identical header-deletion pseudo-label trick, already published at a top-4 security venue. The only conceivable narrowing — bare-metal MCU firmware, where the base genuinely does vary (0x08000000 STM32, 0xBFC00000 MIPS reset, 0x9D000000 PIC32) — fails the manufacturer gate outright: real bare-metal images ship with NO header, so there is nothing to delete and no label to read. You would have to synthesise the corpus yourself with randomised linker scripts, at which point you are teaching a model your own linker-script prior, and the pointer-histogram heuristic recovers it anyway.

HuggingFace has no dataset for this task at any scale (searches for firmware+binary, binary+base+address, raw+binary+architecture all returned zero relevant hits), which is the one thing genuinely missing — but an absent dataset for a task that 13 papers and 2 production tools already solve heuristically is not white space, it is a task nobody needs a dataset for.
round1_leftovers_attacked.g6_reasoning: G6 is the one gate this passes cleanly, and it does not matter. Measured over 725 real ELFs: median 159.3 KiB, mean 749.1 KiB, p90 1393 KiB. Full binaries at 10^6 units = ~0.16 TB, well over the ~30 GB disk. But the task only needs a window: truncating to a 4 KiB byte-window per unit gives 4.1 GB at 10^6, and 16 KiB gives 16 GB — both fit 30 GB disk with the smaller rungs. Models: a 256-bin byte histogram plus n-gram features feeds a linear/GBM classifier that trains on 10^6 rows in minutes on 4 cores; a small 1-D byte-CNN (~1-5 M params, seq len 4096) fits far inside 15 GB and would run maybe 2-6 CPU-hours per epoch at 10^6 on 4 cores, so four rungs at 1k/10k/100k/1M is a few days at most. Feasible. But feasibility is irrelevant when the measured curve is already flat at n=128 and the base-address label carries 0.11 bits conditional on the arch — you would be spending days of CPU to draw a horizontal line.
round1_leftovers_attacked.strongest_case_against: The proposal bundles three sub-tasks and every one of them dies, each to a different gate, so there is no recombination and no rescue. (1) The base-address half — the ONLY reason this candidate survived round 1 — has a label that is a linker constant: measured H(base) = 0.152 bits over 838 multi-arch Debian ELFs, H(base | ISA) = 0.108 bits, and "always predict 0x0" scores 98.45% exact. This is round 1's javac kill in a new costume. (2) The ISA/endianness half is solved to 93.91% by a nearest-centroid on a byte histogram with no training loop, and the measured scaling curve is FLAT from 128 examples onward (91.7% @ 128 → 90.3% @ 523) — four orders of magnitude below the 10^6 target, which inverts the entire FDM-1 thesis. (3) The code/data half is the only one with real residual (dumb baseline 50-56%) and it is verbatim IEEE S&P 2025 LOADSTAR, the same header-deletion pseudo-label trick, published at a top-tier venue. Meanwhile the "asymmetry" is nominal: the deleted header is a redundant copy of information still sitting in the body, which binbloom (585 stars, in production) and six published papers already read back out deterministically — so this is not distillation from a teacher, it is a learned approximation of a solved decoder, which is strictly the worst position to be in. And the buyers named (ONEKEY, NetRise, Binary Ninja) already ship binbloom-class heuristics, so the economic tail is being sold a slower version of what they have. The founder's stated failure mode was building a specialised technique that a general approach matched; here a 10-line non-learned rule matches it, today, at n=128.

round1_leftovers_attacked.a1_channel_capacity: Varies, but carries very few bits, and the residual bits are NOT a function of the input. Measured from CIFP 2608 (parsed 396,460 records -> 93,253 waypoints, 52,404 procedure transitions, 3,070 airports): label cardinality is 3-20 STARs per airport (KJFK 3, KBOS 3, KSEA 4, KMIA 6, KATL 8, KORD 11, KDFW 20, KLAX 20) — roughly 3.3 bits before conditioning. And the classes are geometrically enormous distances apart: pairwise separation between DISTINCT STAR transitions at the same airport has median 44.7-136.4 nm across 14 busy airports, with only 0.0-9.6% of pairs closer than 5 nm and 0.0-3.6% closer than 2 nm (KATL 3,152 pairs: median 77.3 nm, 2.1% within 5 nm; KDEN 5,974 pairs: median 76.1 nm, 0.8% within 5 nm). So the geometry-to-label map is near-deterministic. Where it is NOT — on 27.1% of the cases where the dumb rule disagreed, the two rival published procedures were within 1.0 nm of each other (37.3% within 2.0 nm) — the two candidates occupy essentially the same line in space, so which one ATC actually cleared lives in the flight plan and the clearance, not in lat/lon/alt. That is A1 zero-capacity on precisely the residual the model would have to earn. Worse, 61.7% of real arrivals (731/1185) had no published procedure within 4 nm at all — vectored or off-procedure — and for those the manufacturer produces nothing and nothing can verify a pseudo-label. That is the round-1 crystallography kill repeated: the commercially interesting cases are exactly the ones with no obtainable label.
round1_leftovers_attacked.a2_dumb_baseline: Measured on real data, on this box. Corpus: adsb.lol globe_history 2023-09-01 (ODbL), 1.6 GB streamed and untarred -> 44,742 aircraft traces -> 3,720 real US terminal arrivals at 14 major airports; 1,185 scored against CIFP-derived STAR routes. Dumb baseline = ~40 lines of numpy, no learning: resample each published STAR route (enroute transition + common + runway transition) to 0.5 nm, take mean over route points of min great-circle distance to the trajectory, pick the argmin. (1) As the manufacturer over full trajectories it labels 38.3% of arrivals at fit < 4 nm. (2) As the STUDENT's competitor — the same rule fed only the first 40% of the terminal segment — it recovers the manufacturer's full-trajectory label 395/454 = 87.0% of the time. Median best-vs-second-best margin is 6.77 nm where it agrees and 3.56 nm where it disagrees, and 37.3% of disagreements have rivals within 2 nm. So a non-learned rule with no training data takes 87% of the label, and roughly a third of the remaining 13% is a degenerate label rather than a hard problem. This is the COBOL record-layout pattern from round 1 (50-line rule, F1 0.768) reproduced almost exactly, at a higher number. The curve would be drawn over a ~8-point residual, much of it label noise. Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-raise-v1/5d675fa9-5fc4-501c-b3b3-a76510397d00/scratchpad/parse_cifp.py, geom.py, extract.py, match2.py, match3.py; output in match3.out.
round1_leftovers_attacked.confidence: High. Two independent hard-gate failures, both measured rather than argued, on real data pulled and processed on this box in under an hour: G2a fails because the manufacturer is a public 9 MB file plus a free library function that is fully available at inference time, and the only genuine past-versus-future asymmetry is worth a measured 13 points; A2/G3 fail because a zero-learning 40-line rule takes 87.0% of the label (395/454 real arrivals) while 61.7% of real arrivals cannot be labelled at all and roughly a third of the remaining disagreements are between published procedures lying within 2 nm of each other, i.e. not a function of the input. G4 is separately over budget with eight-plus serious efforts across AIAA, JAIS, IJASS, JOAS and the OpenSky Symposium, an existing open terminal-airspace dataset in Scientific Data 2025, and an existing open toolchain in xoolive/traffic. No narrowing rescues it: the natural narrowings are (i) the vectored 61.7%, which is exactly where the manufacturer produces nothing and where the determining information — the ATC clearance and filed route — is absent from the trajectory; (ii) very-early-prefix prediction before the entry fix, which degenerates into a lookup table over callsign, origin and runway configuration rather than a trajectory model; and (iii) ARINC path-terminator (TF/CF/RF/DF/VA) inference, where CIFP already publishes the leg types for every coded procedure and the distribution is so skewed toward TF that "always TF unless turning" takes most of it. Each narrowed version keeps the buyer and loses the thesis. The residual uncertainty is confined to my matcher's absolute label rate, and correcting that pushes the verdict further toward reject, not away from it.

This includes any and all government and military contractors." The banner at the top of the page repeats it. §3(iii): "You will not distribute, disclose, transfer or otherwise make available the data set(s) to any person other than those employed by your institute" — that alone kills the Phase 3 open artifact. §3(iv): all restrictions propagate to any derived disclosure. §4(ii): "You agree to expunge any and all copies of the received data set(s) upon completion or termination of stated research." §6(i), for commercial licensees: any "invention, discovery, improvement, computer or other program... developed for commercial use by You... shall be the joint property of OpenSky Network and You, and that shared portion is hereby assigned to OpenSky Network" — a default IP-assignment clause that is a company-killer on its own. round1_leftovers_attacked.g2a_what_manufacturer_knows: Almost nothing: the manufacturer is a nearest-polyline match against the FAA CIFP, a 9 MB public file that is equally available to the student and runs in milliseconds at deployment — unlike VPT's IDM, which structurally cannot run at inference — so the only real asymmetry is "manufacturer sees the whole flight, student sees a prefix," and I measured that asymmetry to be worth 13 percentage points (a zero-learning nearest-route rule applied to just the first 40% of the terminal segment already reproduces 87.0% of the full-trajectory label, 395/454 real arrivals).
round1_leftovers_attacked.g3_kill_attempt: Two kill attempts. (a) Frontier general model with plain prompting: this one FAILS to kill. The input is a numeric field (lat/lon/alt/gs/track/vs time series), outside web-text pretraining distribution; plain prompting is not naturally expressible and an LLM has no reason to hold 52,404 CIFP transitions in weights. The G3 heuristic protects this candidate on that axis. (b) Existing non-learned tool: this one KILLS it. xoolive/traffic (PyPI `traffic` 2.13, mature, maintained, free) ships Flight.aligned_on_navpoint(), Flight.aligned_on_ils(), Flight.aligned_on() with method in {'default','beacon','ils','runway'}, LandingAlignedOnILS, RunwayAlignment, and a point_merge algorithm built on aligned_on_navpoint (verified via GitHub code search in src/traffic/core/flight.py and src/traffic/algorithms/navigation/point_merge.py). The entire shape-(c) manufacturer is an off-the-shelf library call over a public 9 MB database. You would be training a neural network to imitate a free deterministic function that anyone can also call at inference time. (c) Scale monotonicity independently: a ~3.3-bit airport-conditioned label over a near-deterministic geometric map saturates fast; the extra 900k examples buy you the vectored tail, whose labels are unverifiable noise. A bigger model does not eat this, but a 40-line function does — which is the same death.
round1_leftovers_attacked.g3_survives: Only this much survives: the input modality is genuinely out of LLM distribution, and the CPU/data engineering is real and cheap. Nothing about the LEARNING thesis survives. The failure mode here is not the founder's old one (bigger model with plain prompting matches it) — it is the adjacent and equally fatal one: a free deterministic tool with no learning matches it, and gets better, not worse, as the manufacturer improves. Note the perverse structure: any improvement to the geometric matcher raises the fraction the free rule labels and therefore SHRINKS the residual the model is supposed to own. The thesis gets worse as the manufacturer gets better, which is the same shape of un-fundability.

round1_leftovers_attacked.g6_reasoning: G6 is the one gate this passes comfortably, which is why it is worth stating plainly that G6 is not the problem. Measured: median real terminal arrival = 184 points (p90 286), so 4.3 KB/unit as raw float32 x 6 channels at native sample rate, or 3.0 KB/unit downsampled to a fixed 128 x 6 float32 tensor -> 3.07 GB for 10^6 units, comfortably inside 23 GB free disk and streamable in shards under 15 GB RAM. Yield: 1.6 GB of one day's adsb.lol tar gave 3,720 US arrivals at 14 airports; extrapolating across all 3,070 CIFP procedure airports, roughly 3-4 x 10^4 US terminal arrivals per day, so ~30 days of the 365-day 2023 archive reaches 10^6 — about 45 GB to download, which needs staged streaming but is workable. Model: a 1-D CNN or small GRU over 128 timesteps x 6 channels with an airport-conditioned softmax over <=20 classes is 1-5 M parameters; that is seconds per epoch at the 1k rung and low single-digit CPU-hours at the 1M rung on 4 cores. Four rungs at 1k/10k/100k/1M in well under a day of compute, with data acquisition the dominant cost. Everything here works. The problem is that the curve it would draw is over an ~8-point residual of a rule that needs no training.
round1_leftovers_attacked.strongest_case_against: My matcher is crude, and I want that on the record. It labels only 38.3% overall and produces obviously broken per-airport rates at KJFK (0%) and KSFO (2%), where real arrivals are almost universally vectored and where my simple concatenation of CIFP transitions plainly under-reconstructs the published routes. A careful manufacturer — using runway configuration, altitude/speed constraints, time-windowed segment matching, and proper ARINC path-terminator expansion for RF/CF/VA legs — would label substantially more than 38.3%. Someone defending this candidate would say my 87% dumb-prefix number is measured on an unrepresentative easy subset. Two answers. First, the 87% is a within-matcher comparison — the same code, same routes, same fit threshold, full trajectory versus 40% prefix — so it is robust to how good the matcher is in absolute terms. Second and decisively, the defence points the wrong way: a BETTER manufacturer labels MORE flights for free and therefore SHRINKS the residual the learned model is supposed to own. Improving the teacher makes the student less necessary. The candidate is squeezed from both sides and there is no matcher quality at which it escapes. The other case against me is G1: I found a real fix (adsb.lol, ODbL) that the pitch missed, so a reviewer could say I should have credited the candidate for a repairable corpus. I did credit it — G1 is marked MARGINAL, not FAIL. It simply is not what kills this. I also could not verify my suspicion that commercial airport noise-monitoring systems (ANOMS, Casper, Topsonic and similar) already ship flight-track-to-published-route correlation as a standard feature, which if true would further erode G5; I did not test it and record it as COULD NOT VERIFY.

screened.overall_read: Not as empty as round 1 — but only just, and the pool is much smaller than 37. After deduplication it is really three structures repeated: (a) an "operational agency revises its own product" family of eight (Sentinel-1 orbits, CO-OPS, USGS, IMERG, altimetry, INTERMAGNET, EPA AQS, AirRef), (b) an "expensive co-located instrument labels a cheap one" family of nine (IonoShape, AuroralFAC, KiK-net, DeepSounding, RepeatSpan, ArterialPPG, SoilLab, SondeProfile, LidarHub), and (c) a "the generator recorded itself" family of twelve (AllocTrace through DAS-Detect). Family (a) is now measured dead as a class, not argued dead. I differenced three real Sentinel-1 RESORB/POEORB arcs (2020-01-02) and a cubic polynomial plus a once-per-revolution sinusoid — no learning, ~10 lines — explains 0.946-0.994 of the residual variance in 8 of 9 component-arcs, and poly5+2cpr leaves 0.03-0.15 cm RMS. The pool's own author guessed 70-90%; the truth is 95-99.9%. That is the same shape as round 1's CO-OPS box-mean result and it should be treated as a general law: smooth reprocessing corrections are fitted, not learned. Family (b) dies on a mix of physics incumbents and licences that forbid redistribution (KiK-net "Re-distribution, selling, and alteration are strictly prohibited"; INTERMAGNET CC BY-NC). Family (c) is where the survivors live, and it has its own general law that this pool discovered and I am adopting: if the generator is analytically invertible, a closed-form inverse takes the whole label (NMR apodization off the reconstructed FID, cryo-EM sharpening off a Guinier plot, halftone screen off a 2-D FFT, aligner off the MAPQ value set). Only lossy, non-invertible generators are candidates. What survives that is genuinely thin — one strong candidate, one promising-but-half-measured, one clean-but-entirely-unmeasured, and one that a 2025 npj paper already published. AllocTrace is the real finding and it is now measured much harder than the pool measured it: on 392,318 California PUMS records (65x the original Wyoming probe) both dumb rules sit at or below chance (AUC 0.374-0.503) against learned AUC 0.89-0.94, and the curve rises monotonically across two full orders of magnitude — but it decelerates badly (mean AUC 0.8873 at n=1k to 0.9251 at n=100k, and only +0.005 over the last half-order). In error-reduction terms it is more respectable than the AUC framing (joint 12-bit exact-match error falls 18.8% relative, Hamming error 15.5%), but nobody should pretend this is a steep curve. The honest bottom line: this pool contains one candidate worth building on and two worth one more week of measurement each, and if the AllocTrace curve does not steepen under the harder framings (cross-state transfer, household context, full 77-bit joint mask) it should be killed rather than defended. Artifacts: /tmp/w/out/scale.log, /tmp/w/out/asm.log, /tmp/w/out/sentinel1_a2.log.
