USGS overwrites provisional with approved and retains only ~120 days of instantaneous values, so the provisional half of every historical pair has been destroyed and no corpus can be built retrospectively. Measured in the pool by an empty instantaneous-values response for site 01646500 on 2015-06-01 against a populated, 'A'-flagged daily-values response for the same dates. Licence was fine; the data is simply gone. This is the canonical screen for structure (a): the early artifact must SURVIVE.

rejected.name: IMERG Early-run to Final-run precipitation correction
rejected.reason: Crowded past the threshold by work that is the task itself. The pool's Crossref query returned as top hit 'IMERG Run Deep: Can we produce a low-latency IMERG Final run product with a deep learning...', with dblp adding 5 satellite-precipitation bias-correction hits and arXiv a dense field (Oya, RainBench, multi-satellite generative frameworks, LSTM merging). At or past three serious efforts. Secondary A2 exposure is real: IMERG's gauge calibration is itself applied as a monthly ratio adjustment, so a per-pixel per-month climatological factor - a lookup table - captures more than half the systematic correction by construction.

rejected.name: ISC preliminary-to-reviewed bulletin phase re-identification
rejected.reason: The analyst's own tooling is the dumb baseline. Comparing observed travel time against ak135 predictions for each candidate phase at the given distance and depth and dropping residual outliers beyond a threshold is a ~50-line rule that recovers most of the re-identification label, and plain identity (keep every reported phase, accept the automatic hypocentre) is right for the large majority of ordinary regional P picks. This is round 1's COBOL shape exactly. Secondary G4 failure: PhaseLink, DECA, GENIE, VORA, HARPA and QuakeFlow already crowd the adjacent association task well past three. Secondary G1: ISC licence text was unreadable and bulk redistribution rights are unresolved, which is fatal for Phase 3 on its own.

rejected.name: BGP announcement to future-adjudicated outcome (RIPE RIS MRT)
rejected.reason: Decisively crowded, measured in the pool: dblp returns 57 hits for 'bgp hijack', Crossref surfaces directly on-target work ('IP Prefix Hijack Detection Using BGP Attack Signatures and Connectivity Tracking', 'BGP prefix hijack detection algorithm based on MOAS event feature'), and ARTEMIS, BGPmon and Cloudflare Radar are production systems doing this today. Secondary A2: the MOAS rule (flag any prefix announced by an origin AS that has not previously originated it) plus a more-specific-than-covering-ROA check is well under 50 lines and is the historical foundation of every hijack detector. Note the useful G1 side-finding: routeviews.org serves 'user-agent: * / disallow: /', a direct A3 hit, while RIPE RIS is clean.

rejected.name: OpenStreetMap edit to future revert-or-correction
rejected.reason: The dumb baseline is metadata, not geometry, and it takes most of the label: contributor edit count, account age, and whether the changeset came from a known bulk import or a game-driven client. Bad OSM edits are heavily concentrated in new accounts and imports, so a reputation-plus-edit-size rule captures most of the revert outcome - and worse, it implies the geometric signal the study would learn is largely redundant. Secondary G3 exposure: OSM tags are human-legible text, which by the mission's own heuristic is where a frontier model eats you. Secondary G4: dblp returns 8 hits on OSM vandalism including four distinct serious efforts (Ovid, attention-based vandalism detection, user-embedding detection, and the 2018 data-driven paper). G1/ODbL was the one clean gate.

rejected.name: MPC Isolated Tracklet File to future orbit linkage
rejected.reason: Corpus not obtainable and the positive class structurally does not survive. itf.txt.gz returns HTTP 404 and minorplanetcenter.net/data returns HTTP 403, so terms were unreadable; more fundamentally, once a tracklet is linked the MPC REMOVES it from the ITF and historical ITF snapshots are not systematically archived, so the early artifact vanishes for exactly the positive examples - the USGS failure in a different costume. Secondary A1, and it is serious: whether a tracklet links depends mostly on how much OTHER data happens to exist for that object (survey cadence, sky coverage, brightness on later nights), so a large part of the label is not a function of the input. Secondary G4: THOR, CANFind and the LSST NEO linking line are three or more serious efforts.

rejected.name: INTERMAGNET provisional-to-definitive geomagnetic baseline
rejected.reason: The label is a spline by construction. The definitive baseline correction is fitted through absolute observations as a smooth piecewise-linear or spline curve, so a per-month constant offset or linear interpolation between month endpoints captures well above 90% of it - the incumbent is literally linear interpolation and it is nearly exact. Secondary A1: the correction carries few effective bits per sample because millions of minute-samples share essentially one number per month, which is the low-dimensional trap dressed as a long time series. Secondary G1: INTERMAGNET is CC BY-NC with per-observatory written-permission requirements for bulk distribution, an A3 kill for a shipped artifact. Secondary G1 again: whether provisional data are retained after definitive release is unverified and historically they are replaced.

rejected.name: EPA AQS preliminary-to-certified hour invalidation
rejected.reason: The early artifact is deliberately destroyed. EPA's own download page states the pre-generated files 'are updated twice per year: once in June to capture the complete data for the prior year and once in December...' - the files are REPLACED, so the preliminary snapshot does not survive alongside the certified one and paired units are effectively zero retrospectively. Public-domain licence was never the problem. Secondary A2 would have bitten anyway: identity (every hour valid) already achieves very high accuracy because invalidation is rare, and a range-plus-rate-of-change rule catches most of the remainder.

rejected.name: TLE epoch to future-TLE-revealed maneuver
rejected.reason: The Space-Track user agreement restricts redistribution to third parties, which is a direct A3 failure for a project whose Phase 3 requires shipping an open artifact; Celestrak redistributes only a subset, so the legally shippable corpus is far below the count that clears G1. Secondary A2, and it is severe on both framings: for detection, thresholding the residual between an SGP4 propagation and the next observed element set finds nearly every maneuver and is the standard operational method; for prediction, a per-satellite station-keeping periodicity rule captures most of the timing. Secondary G4 across three separate domain venues: IEEE Aerospace 2022, the 22nd IAA Symposium on Space Debris, AIAA SciTech 2022, plus NCDE and DQN-LSTM papers on dblp.

rejected.name: TCPState - sender kernel state from a one-directional packet-header trace
rejected.reason: The headline label is exactly computable by arithmetic. From a bidirectional trace, bytes-in-flight - which is cwnd to within one RTT - falls straight out of seq and ack numbers in about twenty lines with no learning. The candidate survives only by deliberately hiding the reverse direction, which is a contrivance any reviewer names on sight, and which simultaneously weakens G2a because the pcap is captured on the same host as the kernel that supplies the label. Rule-based CCA identification also already works well in clean conditions. Secondary G4 over the threshold: Inspector Gadget (TMA 2020), the Gordon-based Great Internet TCP Congestion Control Census (IMC 2019), and the CCAnalyzer/Yeager line, at least four serious efforts. The CC0 licence was the best in the pool and could not save it.

rejected.name: IonoShape - ionosonde profile parameters from ground GNSS slant-TEC fans
rejected.reason: IRI-2020 driven by solar and geomagnetic indices, and the classical M(3000)F2-to-hmF2 empirical formula, already reproduce hmF2 to roughly 10-15% RMS with no learning and without using the TEC input at all. That takes most of the label and leaves a learned model fighting for a few points over a free physics baseline - unfundable. Secondary A1 and it is close to independently disqualifying: slant TEC is a path integral, which is precisely the operation that discards the height information the label encodes, so the channel is partly closed by physics and an early ceiling is expected. Secondary G1: GIRO/DIDBase requires per-station institute contact before publication and bulk redistribution rights are unconfirmed.

rejected.name: AuroralFAC - satellite-measured field-aligned currents from ground magnetometers
rejected.reason: Licence kill as normally sourced, verified in the pool: INTERMAGNET data is CC BY-NC 4.0 - 'provided for non-commercial use', and 'for commercial use or sale or bulk distribution to third parties please obtain written permission from the institute operating the observatory'. That is A3 for both a commercial thesis and a shippable artifact. The public-domain escape hatch is only the 14 USGS observatories, which drops the usable station count from ~600 to 14 and caps the regime diversity the curve could exploit. Secondary A2: a linear regression from the ground H-component onto FAC magnitude captures a large share of the variance because both are driven by the same electrojet. Secondary A1: the spatial inverse (currents above from fields below) is formally ill-posed, so a single station constrains its own footpoint only weakly.

rejected.name: BoreholeSite - bedrock incident motion from a surface accelerograph (KiK-net)
rejected.reason: Hard licence kill, quoted from NIED's own terms: 'Re-distribution, selling, and alteration are strictly prohibited', with registration required to download. Phase 3 requires shipping an open artifact, so this is dead regardless of how good the asymmetry is - and the asymmetry was genuinely excellent (an accelerometer buried in bedrock beneath the site). This is the KiK-net equivalent of round 1's Maven Central finding. Secondary G1: event-station pairs are likely BELOW 1e6 because KiK-net is triggered, not continuous. Secondary A2: a per-station linear transfer function estimated from weak motion and applied by deconvolution is standard engineering practice and recovers most of the label at low shaking levels, leaving only a rare high-amplitude nonlinear tail.

rejected.name: DeepSounding - survey-grade depth from crowdsourced single-beam soundings
rejected.reason: A per-vessel constant offset plus a single linear sound-speed correction - a ~30-line non-learned rule, and exactly what the hydrographic community already does - recovers most of the systematic bias, leaving learning to fight over a residual that is largely irreducible measurement noise. Same shape as round 1's COBOL result. Secondary G1: the NCEI crowdsourced-bathymetry product page returned HTTP 404 so neither the pair count nor the IHO DCDB contributor terms could be verified, and the binding figure is not total soundings but the number OVERLAPPING a multibeam survey, which was never established. Secondary G3: the CSB trusted-node metadata scheme addresses the same problem administratively and for free.

rejected.name: RepeatSpan - tandem-repeat and SV genotype from short-read pileup statistics
rejected.reason: Squarely occupied, five or more serious efforts: ScatTR (2025, 'Estimating the Size of Long Tandem Repeat Expansions from Short-Reads'), STRkit (2025/2026), and the established ExpansionHunter / GangSTR / HipSTR / STRling line, plus deep-learning SV callers. Secondary A2 and it is honest and damaging: the classic mean-insert-size-shift rule formalised in ExpansionHunter already genotypes the overwhelming majority of loci correctly, because ~99% of loci are non-expanded and a rule outputting 'reference length' is right almost always - reporting raw accuracy would be dishonest, and on the expansion tail that actually matters the existing tools are already decent.

rejected.name: ArterialPPG - invasive arterial pressure waveform from a PPG
rejected.reason: One of the most crowded topics in all of biosignal machine learning - cuffless blood pressure from PPG has hundreds of papers, dedicated benchmark corpora (PulseDB), reviews of reviews, and a repeated published finding that reported gains are calibration artefacts. Secondary A2: a two-point per-subject calibration plus a pulse-transit-time linear regression is the standard non-learned clinical baseline and captures a substantial share of within-subject variation, while between subjects the absolute-pressure gain is genuinely unidentifiable from optics alone - which is why this field keeps producing impressive numbers that collapse on new patients. Secondary G1: VitalDB has an unreadable Data Use Agreement and MIMIC requires PhysioNet credentialing with explicit redistribution restrictions, an A3 problem for Phase 3.

rejected.name: SoilLab - destructive lab soil chemistry from MIR spectra
rejected.reason: Abundance fails at the level that matters: OSSL holds ~1e5 spectra with paired lab values, and while multiplying by 50 properties reaches 1e6-1e7 (spectrum, property) pairs, INDEPENDENT units stay at ~1e5, so the required 1k/10k/100k/1M rungs cannot be spanned. Secondary A2 is independently fatal: PLS regression on the raw spectrum, a 1980s technique with no deep learning, already achieves most of the achievable accuracy for organic carbon and texture, with a reported gap to modern ML of a few percent. Secondary G4: EuropePMC returns 63 hits for the narrow phrase 'soil spectroscopy' AND 'machine learning' alone. The CC-BY-4.0 licence was the one clean gate.

rejected.name: AirRef - reference-monitor concentration from a low-cost air-quality sensor
rejected.reason: Textbook A2 failure: the dumb rule is not merely close, it IS the accepted operational standard. The published US EPA correction for PurpleAir is literally a two-term humidity-corrected formula, and it captures the large majority of the correctable error. Secondary G3: the relationship is a smooth low-dimensional function of (raw, T, RH) with few effective degrees of freedom, so the curve flattens fast regardless of volume. Secondary G4, verified: EuropePMC returns 946 hits for 'low-cost sensor' AND calibration, including 2026 work on remotely calibrating a nationwide dense network. Secondary G1: PurpleAir API terms restrict bulk use and redistribution.

rejected.name: SondeProfile - radiosonde vertical profile from ground GNSS delay plus surface met
rejected.reason: The label is largely not a function of the input. One scalar path-integrated delay plus surface values cannot determine a vertical profile - integration is exactly the operation that collapses the height distribution the label encodes - so the channel to profile SHAPE is nearly closed. Secondary A2: a climatological mean profile for that station, month and hour rescaled to match the observed integrated water vapour, i.e. the standard Askne-Nordius/GPT approach with no learning, is genuinely hard to beat by much. Secondary G3: the real incumbent is numerical weather prediction, which assimilates the GNSS delay along with everything else - any buyer with internet access already has ERA5 and a better profile than a single-station model can produce.

rejected.name: LidarHub - hub-height wind and turbulence from surface anemometry
rejected.reason: Killed by a pincer in which A1 and A2 fail in complementary regimes, so no regime is left to win. In convective daytime conditions surface and rotor layers are well coupled, so capacity is high - but that is exactly where the power-law/log-law shear extrapolation, the wind industry's standard non-learned method, already works well. On stable nights the layers decouple and the physical channel is close to severed, so the label stops being a function of the input precisely when the buyer cares most. Secondary G1: ~1e6 usable pairs is borderline before availability filtering, ARM's specific policy URLs returned 404, and redistribution of a derived artifact is unverified. Secondary G5: an operator who cares enough simply deploys their own lidar.

rejected.name: CallerPrint - recovering the variant caller and its filter thresholds from a VCF
rejected.reason: Label diversity fails even though record counts do not. Variant-record units number ~1e9 across gnomAD alone, but the label is per-call-set and distinct LABELLED call sets are plausibly only 1e3-1e4, so the effective label diversity cannot span 1k/10k/100k/1M - the same failure I am applying to RefinePrint-PDB. Worse, the ##source header is frequently absent or uninformative in public call sets, so the labelled subset is smaller still and was never enumerated. Secondary A2 by the pool's own honest estimate: six or seven rules ('emits MNPs => FreeBayes', 'indels not left-aligned => older bcftools', 'no calls in homopolymers over length N => hard-filtered GATK') get the caller family most of the time. Secondary G4 of the right kind: GA4GH, hap.py and GIAB have published exactly how callers differ, so a rules engine built from that literature is a credible incumbent no amount of data beats. Kept in the pool as a backup behind AssemblyProv; not promoted.

rejected.name: AlignerPrint - recovering the read aligner from BAM alignment records
rejected.reason: A five-line rule reads the label off directly. The set of MAPQ values an aligner can emit is a fingerprint - bowtie2 caps at 42, bwa-mem at 60, and each has a characteristic discrete value set - so collecting the distinct MAPQ values observed in a few thousand records identifies the aligner family with near-certainty and no learning whatsoever, with soft-clip presence adding a second free bit. What remains is parameter-level inference on a task nobody is paying for. Note the secondary G2a weakness the pool correctly flagged: the aligner's identity is stamped INTO the records rather than held back, which is the opposite of the asymmetry this study needs.

rejected.name: FactType-XBRL - recovering the taxonomy element from unlabelled numeric facts
rejected.reason: This is semantic column-type detection wearing a finance costume, and that field is heavily worked: Sherlock (KDD 2019), Sato, TURL, DoDuo and the SemTab challenge series are all directly applicable and several explicitly handle numeric-only columns - well over three serious efforts. The pool's dblp queries returned near-zero, and it correctly overrode its own query results with known literature rather than claiming false white space; I endorse that override. Secondary A2: a rule keyed on order of magnitude, sign and the 'decimals' attribute separates the coarse families (balance-sheet totals vs per-share vs ratios vs share counts) with no learning, so any headline accuracy would be badly inflated by easy classes. Secondary: the task is somewhat artificial since element names are present in practice.

rejected.name: RefinePrint-PDB - recovering the refinement protocol from atomic coordinates
rejected.reason: Abundance fails at the label level, verified via the RCSB search API: total_count = 258,616 entries. The label is per-entry, so effective label diversity is 2.6e5, which cannot span rungs ending at 1e6; reformulating at residue level would give ~6e7 units but shares one label across thousands of residues, weakening rather than fixing it. Secondary A2 moderate: bond-length RMSD against the Engh-Huber library plus the autocorrelation of B-factors along the chain (TLS refinement produces conspicuously smooth group-wise B-factors) is a two-threshold rule that gets maybe half the coarse label. Secondary G3: MolProbity and PDB-REDO already compute exactly these geometry statistics as their core function, so a well-engineered validation-report incumbent exists.

rejected.name: SpecProc-NMR - recovering the processing parameters from a processed NMR spectrum
rejected.reason: A closed-form inverse takes the entire label, and this is the candidate that establishes the general law for the whole 'generator still exists' structure. Inverse-Fourier-transform the spectrum back to the time domain and the apodization window is sitting there as the visible envelope of the reconstructed FID - read it off by fitting an exponential or sine-bell in about twenty lines. Zero-filling is read directly from point count versus acquisition time; phase correction is recovered by any standard automatic phasing routine. Because the generator is deterministic and very nearly invertible, G2a is illusory (verdict FAIL) - the manufacturer holds nothing the student cannot reconstruct. No amount of data raises a curve above a closed-form inverse. Secondary G1: BMRB labelled spectra are likely ~1e4, far under the bar.

rejected.name: SharpenProv-EM - recovering the sharpening and symmetry from a cryo-EM density map
rejected.reason: Same closed-form-inverse kill as SpecProc-NMR. Sharpening is applied as exp(-B*s^2/4) in reciprocal space, so a Guinier plot of the map's radial power spectrum recovers B directly from the slope - a textbook thirty-line operation that is the literal inverse of the generator. Imposed point-group symmetry is recovered by rotational cross-correlation of the map with itself over candidate groups, a standard deterministic search that succeeds essentially always. Between them the two dumb procedures take the whole label, and G2a is correspondingly FAIL. Secondary G1: EMDB holds on the order of 1e4-1e5 maps, far under 1e6. Secondary G6: voxel grids are too large for a 4-core, 15GB, 30GB-disk box at 1e6 units.

rejected.name: ScreenProv - recovering the RIP screening parameters from a halftoned raster
rejected.reason: A single 2-D FFT of the raster puts the screen angle and line frequency at the spectral peaks - a ten-line non-learned procedure that recovers the parameters to high precision for the AM case, which is nearly all of the label space. Only stochastic/FM screening resists it, which narrows the candidate to a sliver. Secondary G1, independently fatal: no public corpus of halftoned rasters with recorded RIP settings exists, so the corpus would have to be self-generated by running Ghostscript, at which point the 'generator still exists' framing collapses into simulation and real-world labelled units are zero. Secondary G4: a 2011 IEEE paper on parameter estimation for AM halftone images is direct prior art. Secondary G6: rasters are bulky for the box.

rejected.name: CRDSProv - recovering the calibration reference files used on a space-telescope exposure
rejected.reason: Textbook javac shape and the prior from round 1 says candidates of this exact shape fail. Calibration is DESIGNED to remove the reference file's imprint; if it succeeds, the calibrated pixels carry near-zero information about which dark or flat was subtracted and the label is not a function of the input - the same zero-capacity failure that killed JVM build-provenance when 345 of 345 class files came back byte-identical. The optimistic case (imperfect calibration leaving epoch-specific hot-pixel populations and CTE trails) is entirely unmeasured, and the required test is the direct analogue of the 345-of-345 comparison. Conditional on A1 passing, A2 would actually be fine, but that condition does all the work. Secondary G6: not feasible at 1e6 units without severe patch subsampling since full frames are megapixels. Secondary G5: MAST serves the header for free, so the buyer is thin - only orphaned or third-party-reprocessed data.

rejected.name: DEMProc - recovering the stereo-matching parameters from a photogrammetric DEM
rejected.reason: Redistribution is not permitted. ArcticDEM is governed by the Electro-Optical Commercial Layer (EOCL) contract with a PGC acknowledgement policy rather than an open licence, because it is derived from commercial Maxar imagery, and Alaska coverage was restricted after June 2022 - so shipping a derived training artifact, which Phase 3 requires, is not clearly allowed. This is precisely the A3 pattern: fetchable is not redistributable. Secondary G1: 605,596 strip DEMs is below 1e6 at the label level, and sub-strip patches share a strip's label. Secondary A2: if matching window size is the main label, the break frequency of the elevation noise power spectrum reads it off via a one-line FFT-and-fit - the same closed-form-inverse failure as NMR and cryo-EM. Secondary G6: rasters are too bulky for the box.

rejected.name: DAS-Detect - detecting disclosure-control perturbation in published statistics
rejected.reason: Zero capacity BY DESIGN, with a mathematical proof attached - the cleanest negative in the set and the boundary case that clarifies the whole structure. Differential privacy is a guarantee that the released table reveals a bounded amount about the true counts, and the noise is drawn independently of the data precisely so that no function of the release can recover it; the label is provably close to not being a function of the input, with capacity capped by an epsilon parameter. This is the javac failure with a theorem. Secondary A2 for the legacy rounding case: 'value is a multiple of 5 => rounded' takes the entire label instantly. Worth keeping on the record because it is the exact inverse of its sibling AllocTrace, which survives precisely because the Census PUBLISHES the imputation flags rather than hiding them - the label exists and is free while the pre-imputation input is genuinely destroyed.

survivors.a2_dumb_baseline: MEASURED AT 392,318 RECORDS AND IT GETS NOTHING - the cleanest A2 pass in either round. Rule 1 ('value is zero or blank => allocated'): AUC 0.3758 (FWAGP), 0.3905 (FPINCP), 0.4852 (FSCHLP), 0.5000 (FHICOVP), 0.5025 (FAGEP), 0.4856 (FINTP), 0.3739 (FPERNP), 0.5000 (FHINS1P), 0.5000 (FPUBCOVP). Rule 2 ('value equals the modal value => allocated'): 0.3758 / 0.3905 / 0.4494 / 0.4989 / 0.5012 / 0.4856 / 0.3739 / 0.4785 / 0.4191. Every one is at or BELOW chance, against learned AUC 0.886-0.939 on the same flags. This replicates the pool's Wyoming result at 65x scale, on a different state, with no softening. The mechanism is why: hot-deck donors are drawn from real reported values, so an allocated entry is not blanker, rounder, or more modal than a reported one - several rules are anti-correlated, meaning allocated values are LESS likely to be zero than reported ones. The signal lives in subtle joint implausibility across correlated fields, which no ~50-line rule expresses. Round 1's COBOL failure mode is decisively absent here.
survivors.g1_corpus: US Census Bureau ACS PUMS bulk files on www2.census.gov. VERIFIED BY DOWNLOAD THIS ROUND: csv_pca.zip (2023 1-Year, California) = 69,791,730 bytes, unpacks to psam_p06.csv with 392,318 person records, 287 columns, of which 77 are contiguous allocation flags (FAGEP..FYOEP). Flag rates are substantial and non-degenerate: FPINCP 0.275, FHICOVP 0.236, FPUBCOVP 0.229, FPRIVCOVP 0.225, FHINS7P 0.220, ... 56+ flags fire above 2%. One state-year alone is 3.9e5 units; 50 states x 20 years of 1-year files plus the 5-year files put the national corpus at ~1e7 person records and ~7.7e8 binary flag labels.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The Census Bureau's hot-deck edit-and-allocation system generated the released record from the raw questionnaire and RECORDS ITS OWN ACTIONS as the F* flag columns, published in the same CSV. Label manufacture is a column split: keep the 77 flag columns as y, delete them from X. Marginal cost is exactly zero - the labels ship inside the corpus, already paid for by the federal statistical system.
survivors.g2a_asymmetry: The manufacturer saw the respondent's original questionnaire - the blank, contradictory, or out-of-range entry that triggered allocation - which is destroyed by law and never released, while the student sees only the post-imputation record in which every field is populated and internally consistent.
survivors.g3_argument: The input is a vector of integer survey codes with no natural-language surface, so a frontier model cannot be prompted on it in any expressible way; even handed the codebook, the task is a joint-plausibility judgement over 77 correlated coded fields, not a reading task. The failure mode that killed the founder's last company - a bigger model with plain prompting matching a specialised technique - is not available to an attacker here. MEASURED SCALING on California, 80,000 held-out test records, 12 most common flags, HistGradientBoosting: n=1,000 mean AUC 0.8873 / joint 12-bit exact-match 0.6649 / Hamming err 0.1128; n=3,000 0.8981 / 0.6784 / 0.1078; n=10,000 0.9124 / 0.7087 / 0.1004; n=30,000 0.9201 / 0.7243 / 0.0971; n=100,000 0.9251 / 0.7280 / 0.0953. Monotone across two full orders of magnitude with no reversal; joint exact-match error falls 18.8% relative and Hamming error 15.5% relative over that span. HONEST WEAKNESS, STATED AT FULL SIZE: the curve is decelerating hard - the last half-order (30k to 100k) buys only +0.005 mean AUC and +0.004 exact-match, and a per-flag GBM will very likely saturate near 0.93-0.95 well before 1e6. This candidate's scaling story therefore has to live in the harder framings that were NOT measured: the full 77-bit joint mask, cross-state and cross-year transfer, and person-plus-household joint context. If those also flatten by 1e5, kill it rather than defend it. That test is a day's work and should be the first thing Phase 1 does.

arXiv full-text: all:"allocation flags" - MEASURED, 0 entries; all:"imputation" AND all:"census microdata" - MEASURED, 1 entry (A Total Statistical Error Framework for Comparing Census Data Collection Methods), not the task

Crossref practitioner phrasing: 'predicting item nonresponse allocation' - MEASURED, closest hit is 'Prediction of Survey Item Nonresponse Through Supervised Machine Learning' (2025), which predicts whether a respondent will fail to answer from paradata, NOT recovery of the imputation mask from a released record. Follow this one paper up in full before committing - it is the only adjacent serious effort found.

GitHub repository search: 'PUMS allocation flag imputation detection' - MEASURED THIS ROUND, total_count 0

Domain-specific venue 1 - survey methodology: search Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology, Journal of Official Statistics, and the Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) research conference proceedings for 'allocation rate', 'edit and imputation evaluation', 'imputation flag'. This is the venue where the incumbent lives and it was NOT checked by the pool.

Domain-specific venue 2 - statistical disclosure control: UNECE/Eurostat Work Session on Statistical Data Confidentiality and PSD (Privacy in Statistical Databases) proceedings for 'imputation leakage', 'attribute disclosure from imputed values'. If anyone has framed mask recovery as an attack, it is here.
survivors.g5_buyer: National statistical offices and their commercial redistributors - the Census Bureau's own Disclosure Review Board, ONS and Eurostat equivalents, and social-science data archives such as IPUMS - who need to audit how much of a published table is real response versus machine fill before certifying it.
survivors.input_modality: Fixed-width vector of ~124 integer/categorical survey codes per person (age, income, insurance, occupation, migration). No natural-language surface, no image; alphanumeric industry/occupation codes are integer-encoded.
survivors.name: AllocTrace - recovering the census imputation mask from released microdata
survivors.one_line: Given a US Census ACS PUMS person record with its allocation flags deleted, predict which fields the Census edit-and-imputation system filled in rather than the respondent reporting.
survivors.output_label: A 77-bit allocation mask, one binary flag per variable, published in the same file. Framable per-flag (binary), as a joint mask (exact-match over 2^77), or as a count.
survivors.why_survives: It is the only candidate in either round where A1, A2 and the scaling curve are all measured rather than argued, and where the dumb baseline was measured BELOW CHANCE. G2a is airtight and unusual: the manufacturer's private information (the raw questionnaire) is destroyed by federal law, so no amount of model scale can recover it from the student's side - this is not distillation, and there is no teacher to be a ceiling. G1 is verified by download with a permissive robots.txt (www2.census.gov serves 'User-agent: *' with no Disallow) and the bulk files are uncopyrighted federal works, so Phase 3 redistribution is clean. G6 is trivial: the entire probe above ran on this 4-core box in minutes, and 1e6 records is ~1GB as float32. The single reason not to lead with it would be the deceleration, which is real, measured, and stated - not hidden. survivors.a2_dumb_baseline: MEASURED THIS ROUND AND IT IS A REAL TAX, BUT NOT FATAL. I trained a gradient-boosted model on ONLY the QUAST-style contiguity statistics any bioinformatician computes for free (number_of_contigs, contig_n50, contig_l50, total length, gc_percent, number_of_scaffolds, scaffold_n50, ungapped length, plus n50/length, contigs-per-Mb, and an N-content proxy) - this is the honest dumb baseline, the rules-plus-QUAST incumbent. Results on the 178,707-assembly corpus: 18-class assembler FAMILY, ACC 0.745 / balanced-ACC 0.461 against a majority baseline of 0.367; 20-class VERSION STRING, ACC 0.786 / bal-ACC 0.559 (majority 0.350); 19 SPAdes versions only, ACC 0.546 / bal-ACC 0.509 (majority 0.124); 4-class technology, ACC 0.956 but majority is already 0.932 and bal-ACC only 0.560. Reading this honestly: the coarse technology label is near-degenerate (93% Illumina) and must be DISCARDED, not reported as a win. Family is half-solved by free statistics - 26 points of headroom on raw accuracy, more on balanced. The defensible target is the fine-grained one: 19-way SPAdes version leaves ~45 points of headroom over free statistics, and genome coverage as a regression target was not touchable by them at all. Note one confound that runs in the dumb baseline's favour and must be controlled: assembler version correlates with deposit date and submitting lab, so a fair version-level split must be time-blocked.
survivors.g1_corpus: NCBI GenBank via the Datasets API. VERIFIED BY BULK PULL THIS ROUND: 178,707 labelled GenBank bacterial assemblies retrieved across 10 taxa (S. aureus, E. coli, M. tuberculosis, S. Typhi, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Enterococcus, Klebsiella, S. pneumoniae, Neisseria), every one carrying a non-empty assembly_method string. Label distribution measured: SPAdes 59,455 / SKESA 35,614 / Prokka 25,845 / Unicycler 8,328 / allpaths 6,340 / Velvet 4,430 / CLC NGS Cell 4,231 / SOAPdenovo 3,466, with 3,517 DISTINCT version strings. Ten taxa yield 1.8e5 labelled units, so the 3.8e6-assembly archive plausibly holds >1e6 labelled - and the label diversity (3,517 version strings) is the number that matters and it is large.
survivors.g2_mechanism: The assembler mechanically generated the contig set from a read set under a specific parameterisation, and the submitter's structured comment records the generator. Label manufacture is parsing the ##Genome-Assembly-Data## block out of the flatfile (or reading assembly_info from the Datasets API, as I did) and stripping it from the input. The corpus is self-labelling; marginal cost per label is one JSON field access.
survivors.g2a_asymmetry: The manufacturer knows the read set and the assembler invocation - the coverage depth, the platform's error profile, the k-mer size and the assembly graph that was actually traversed - none of which survive into the contig sequences the student is given, because assembly is a lossy many-to-one collapse of reads onto consensus.
survivors.g3_argument: DNA sequence is not web text and a frontier model has no prompt-expressible route to 'which assembler built this contig set' - the input is megabases of ACGT. Scale monotonicity is plausible on mechanism: the discriminating evidence is rare local events (repeat-collapse boundaries, coverage-driven graph breaks, the exact position where the assembler gave up), each assembly contributes a handful, and the label space is large (3,517 measured version strings), so characterising the tail genuinely needs volume rather than saturating on the first thousand genomes. The threat is not a bigger model; the threat is QUAST plus a decision tree, and I have now measured exactly how much that threat gets.

survivors.why_survives: It survives because the measurement I ran came back the way the candidate needed and against the pool author's own pessimism: the free-statistics baseline does NOT take the fine-grained label. THE ONE THING STILL UNMEASURED IS THE THING THE WHOLE CANDIDATE RESTS ON: whether the NUCLEOTIDES carry signal beyond the contig-length multiset. It is possible that everything is in the lengths, in which case this collapses into the dumb baseline I just measured. That test - pull ~500 assemblies from two assemblers at matched taxon and N50, and ask whether contig-boundary sequence adds over lengths alone - is one afternoon and ~2GB, and it must be run BEFORE anything else. survivors.a2_dumb_baseline: ENTIRELY UNMEASURED THIS ROUND AND THIS IS THE CANDIDATE'S WHOLE RISK. The dumb baseline is embarrassingly strong on its face: the broadcast URA/SISA index is the operator's own error bound, shipped free inside the student's input, and a per-satellite mean |SISRE| scaled linearly by age-of-data is a ~15-line lookup table that is roughly what industry uses today. My honest prior is that it captures around half the variance of |SISRE|. The learnable margin is specifically the conditional TAIL - the 99.9th-percentile bound that drives aviation and autonomy protection levels - where URA is a loose per-satellite constant that tracks neither eclipse-season yaw maneuvers, nor upload cadence, nor clock-model drift. THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT: one month of BRDC plus SP3, about a 1 GB download and an afternoon, gives the |SISRE| distribution stratified by URA index and age-of-data. If the URA lookup explains most of the tail as well as the mean, this dies exactly as Sentinel-1 died to a polynomial today. Do not commit a week to this before running that.
survivors.g1_corpus: Daily merged broadcast navigation files (BRDC RINEX) joined to precise orbit/clock products (SP3/CLK) by satellite and epoch. ~110 active satellites x ~12 nav records/day x a decade is ~4.8e6 (record, error-trajectory) pairs and ~1e8 satellite-epochs at 5-minute label granularity. Storage is ~10-20 GB for a decade of raw and a few hundred MB after feature reduction. VERIFIED THIS ROUND: HuggingFace returns 0 datasets for 'GNSS ephemeris'/'broadcast ephemeris'/'SP3 orbit'/'RINEX' shaped this way (the 8 GNSS hits are RTK NMEA logs, jamming recordings and SLAM evaluation sets), and GitHub returns 0 repositories. NOT VERIFIED THIS ROUND: I did not download a BRDC/SP3 pair. NASA CDDIS robots.txt is 'Disallow: /archive' and BKG's mirror is 'Disallow: /root_ftp/' - neither may be crawled; the sanctioned routes are CDDIS's Earthdata-authenticated HTTPS and ESA GSSC (robots.txt permissive, only /wp-admin/), and I confirmed gssc.esa.int and navigation-office.esa.int return 200 but did not locate the exact daily-archive path.
survivors.g2_mechanism: Propagate each broadcast record's Keplerian and clock model to a grid of epochs, difference against the precise SP3/CLK at the same epochs in the same frame with antenna-phase-centre and time-system offsets applied, emit the error trajectory. One-time download of a few GB, then zero marginal cost per label forever. This is exactly the differencing that produces the published SISRE statistics the constellations report.
survivors.g2a_asymmetry: The manufacturer sees where the satellite actually went and what its clock actually did, reconstructed days afterwards from a ~500-station global tracking network, while the student sees only the ground segment's forward prediction, broadcast hours before that truth existed.
survivors.g3_argument: The input is a binary/numeric orbital-element block. A frontier LLM with plain prompting cannot express Keplerian propagation, ECEF frame rotation and error-quantile estimation over it - the task is not merely hard for prompting, it is not expressible, which is precisely the property the founder needs after his last company was matched by plain prompting on a 3x model. Scale monotonicity has a clean mechanism: the payload is a rare-event tail (bad uploads, clock jumps, eclipse-season yaw, maneuvers), so the quantile estimate at 99.9% is data-starved by construction and should keep improving with years and constellations long after the mean saturates. This is the one candidate whose target metric is intrinsically tail-shaped, which is the best available defence against the flattening that is visibly threatening AllocTrace.

survivors.why_survives: It survives on the two gates that killed most of the pool. G2a is the cleanest in the whole set and is the closest structural analogue to VPT anywhere here: the manufacturer literally observes the future the student is being asked to predict, reconstructed from a global network the student has no access to, and no scaling of a general model closes that gap. G4 is genuinely white and I measured it: dblp returns 2 hits for 'broadcast ephemeris error' and both are characterisation studies (Galileo error analysis 2017-2020; real-time PPP), 1 hit for 'signal in space range error' (a pseudolite paper), 0 for 'GNSS integrity machine learning'; arXiv's only SISRE hit is a BeiDou-3 quality assessment; no open dataset and no GitHub repo. G6 is ideal - ~100-float units, four rungs in minutes to hours on 4 cores with no GPU. G1 has a clean redistribution path that most of this pool lacks: GPS broadcast navigation messages and NGA precise GPS ephemerides are US Government works with no copyright, so a GPS-only shipped artifact is safe, and Galileo/BeiDou can be added later after their own terms check. It ranks third only because everything about its A2 is argument rather than measurement, and today's Sentinel-1 result is a reminder of what happens to unmeasured A2 arguments in this exact structure - smooth-physics domains where the incumbent is a fitted curve.

survivors.a2_dumb_baseline: GENUINELY WEAK, WHICH IS THIS CANDIDATE'S ONE REAL STRENGTH AND THE REASON IT IS HERE AT ALL. The obvious non-learned rule - read the model off its native grid spacing and land-sea mask - is a giveaway, but it is defeated by design: regrid every field to a common coarse grid before the student sees it, which the study must do anyway. After regridding, the remaining dumb rules are climatological bias thresholds (mean temperature offset, global precipitation total), which separate a handful of outlier models and leave the bulk indistinguishable. Unlike SpecProc-NMR, SharpenProv-EM, ScreenProv and AlignerPrint - all of which died today or in the pool to a closed-form inverse or a five-line fingerprint - there is no analytic inverse from a field slice back to a model identity. UNMEASURED by me; the regridding defence in particular needs to be demonstrated rather than assumed, because if any residual grid artefact survives interpolation the whole thing collapses to a one-line rule.

survivors.why_survives: It survives literally rather than comfortably, and it is included as a hedge, not a recommendation. It passes every hard gate as written: G2a is real, A2 is weak after regridding (rare in this pool), A1 is established non-zero by prior work rather than assumed, the input is numeric so G3's frontier-model failure mode is unavailable, and G4 returns exactly one serious effort, which is under the ~3 threshold. THREE HONEST REASONS IT RANKS LAST, STATED AT FULL SIZE. First, that one effort - 'Using artificial intelligence to identify CMIP6 models from daily SLP maps', npj Climate and Atmospheric Science 2025, which I confirmed via Crossref this round - IS the task. It is not adjacent. A funder's first question will be what this adds, and the only honest answer is 'the scaling curve, which they did not produce'. Second, that same paper reports the result collapsing seasonally (strong in summer, sharply worse in winter), which says the ceiling is set by irreducible internal variability rather than by data volume - the flattening risk that the founder specifically cannot afford, and here it is already documented in the literature rather than merely suspected. Third, G1 is the weakest of the four survivors: CMIP6 licensing is mixed and a non-trivial minority of modelling groups use CC-BY-NC, which is incompatible with both a commercial thesis and a shipped open artifact, so the corpus must be filtered per source_id before anything is redistributed - and I did not verify that split. Promote this only if the AllocTrace joint-mask curve flattens and the AssemblyProv nucleotide test fails.
